answer: The strongest lever is simple: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because nadir only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, tide is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any marble approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
